# Spirit of the Whitelist
Yautja are antagonists, but should use common sense when hunting during a round and be aware of their surroundings. They should not be detrimental to the round or to the whitelist as a whole.
The Honor Code realistically covers only a small portion of the events and scenarios Yautja may encounter. Use its set-in-stone rules to guide your judgement in situations it does not clearly define, so that you act in a way that befits a whitelisted Yautja.
[color=#ffbf00][bold]Staff hold the final say and can remove you if they believe you are not acting in the Spirit of the Whitelist.[/bold][/color] Every case is handled individually and won't be used for grudges.
## Good examples - Sparing, or throwing back, revivable prey who fought well. - Gifting someone a spear or a gear piece after they kill a Yautja, even outside of a duel. - Making someone's day: thralling a new player, making a fighting pit, creating an interesting roleplay situation. - Stalking, or otherwise taking your time to roleplay, so each hunt feels special and unique. - Sparing, or throwing back, prey that showed good roleplay.
## Bad examples - Placing hunting traps on a road leading out of the FOB and attacking anybody who walks into them. - Lethal plasma casting a regular marine just because they are hunting you down. - Murdering someone instantly because they are holding gear groundside. - Round removing someone who shoots at you while you are cloaked. - Making a show of getting as many kills as possible within a round. - Baiting honor duels with other Yautja to show off mechanical superiority.
